# Overview

```{python}
#| include: false
#| label: imports
import json
import uuid

import altair as alt
import pandas as pd

from altair.datasets import data


# This page mixes Altair (Vega) charts with Observable JS (OJS) cells. Adding OJS
# makes Quarto load RequireJS, which sends Altair's default HTML renderer down its
# AMD branch, where "vega-embed" no longer resolves to the callable embed function
# -> "vegaEmbed is not a function" and every chart fails to render.
#
# Fix: a custom renderer that embeds each chart with a native ES-module <script>
# (`import embed from ".../vega-embed@7/+esm"`). ES modules use the browser's own
# loader, which is completely independent of RequireJS/AMD, so the OJS/RequireJS
# conflict disappears while charts keep full interactivity (tooltips, selections).
def esm_vega_renderer(spec, **metadata):
    div_id = "vega-" + uuid.uuid4().hex
    spec_json = json.dumps(spec)
    html = (
        f'<div id="{div_id}" class="vega-embed-esm"></div>\n'
        f'<script type="module">\n'
        f'  import embed from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vega-embed@7/+esm";\n'
        f'  embed(document.getElementById("{div_id}"), {spec_json}, {{actions: true}})\n'
        f'    .catch((err) => console.error("vega-embed error:", err));\n'
        f'</script>'
    )
    return {"text/html": html}


alt.renderers.register("esm", esm_vega_renderer)
alt.renderers.enable("esm")


#import itables
#itables.init_notebook_mode(all_interactive=True)


```

# Exploratory Story

```{python}
#| include: false
#| label: exploratory-setup
import re

alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows()

centers = data_centers.copy()
timeline = datasets.data_center_timelines()

POWER = "Current power (MW)"
H100 = "Current H100 equivalents"
CAPEX = "Current total capital cost (2025 USD billions)"

for col in [POWER, H100, CAPEX]:
    centers[col] = pd.to_numeric(centers[col], errors="coerce")

timeline["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(timeline["Date"], errors="coerce")
for col in [
    "Power (MW)",
    "H100 equivalents",
    "Total capital cost (2025 USD billions)",
]:
    timeline[col] = pd.to_numeric(timeline[col], errors="coerce")


def clean_party(value):
    if pd.isna(value):
        return "Unknown"
    text = str(value).split(",")[0]
    text = re.sub(r"#\w+", "", text).strip()
    checks = [
        ("Google", "Google"),
        ("Microsoft", "Microsoft"),
        ("Amazon", "Amazon"),
        ("AWS", "Amazon"),
        ("Meta", "Meta"),
        ("Facebook", "Meta"),
        ("SpaceXAI", "xAI"),
        ("xAI", "xAI"),
        ("Oracle", "Oracle"),
        ("OpenAI", "OpenAI"),
        ("Anthropic", "Anthropic"),
        ("CoreWeave", "CoreWeave"),
        ("Tesla", "Tesla"),
    ]
    for needle, label in checks:
        if needle.lower() in text.lower():
            return label
    return text or "Unknown"


STATE_NAMES = {
    "Alabama": "AL",
    "Alaska": "AK",
    "Arizona": "AZ",
    "Arkansas": "AR",
    "California": "CA",
    "Colorado": "CO",
    "Connecticut": "CT",
    "Delaware": "DE",
    "Florida": "FL",
    "Georgia": "GA",
    "Hawaii": "HI",
    "Idaho": "ID",
    "Illinois": "IL",
    "Indiana": "IN",
    "Iowa": "IA",
    "Kansas": "KS",
    "Kentucky": "KY",
    "Louisiana": "LA",
    "Maine": "ME",
    "Maryland": "MD",
    "Massachusetts": "MA",
    "Michigan": "MI",
    "Minnesota": "MN",
    "Mississippi": "MS",
    "Missouri": "MO",
    "Montana": "MT",
    "Nebraska": "NE",
    "Nevada": "NV",
    "New Hampshire": "NH",
    "New Jersey": "NJ",
    "New Mexico": "NM",
    "New York": "NY",
    "North Carolina": "NC",
    "North Dakota": "ND",
    "Ohio": "OH",
    "Oklahoma": "OK",
    "Oregon": "OR",
    "Pennsylvania": "PA",
    "Rhode Island": "RI",
    "South Carolina": "SC",
    "South Dakota": "SD",
    "Tennessee": "TN",
    "Texas": "TX",
    "Utah": "UT",
    "Vermont": "VT",
    "Virginia": "VA",
    "Washington": "WA",
    "West Virginia": "WV",
    "Wisconsin": "WI",
    "Wyoming": "WY",
}
STATE_ABBRS = set(STATE_NAMES.values())


def extract_state(row):
    if row.get("Country") != "United States":
        return "Non-U.S."
    text = " ".join(
        str(row.get(col, ""))
        for col in ["Address", "Name", "Notes"]
        if pd.notna(row.get(col, pd.NA))
    )
    abbr_match = re.search(r"\b(" + "|".join(sorted(STATE_ABBRS)) + r")\b", text)
    if abbr_match:
        return abbr_match.group(1)
    for name, abbr in STATE_NAMES.items():
        if re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(name) + r"\b", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
            return abbr
    return "Unknown"


centers["owner_clean"] = centers["Owner"].map(clean_party)
centers["user_clean"] = centers["Users"].map(clean_party)
centers["state"] = centers.apply(extract_state, axis=1)
centers["continent"] = centers["Country"].map(
    {
        "United States": "North America",
        "Malaysia": "Asia",
        "China": "Asia",
        "Indonesia": "Asia",
        "Portugal": "Europe",
        "United Arab Emirates": "Asia",
    }
).fillna("Other")
centers["h100_per_mw"] = centers[H100] / centers[POWER]
centers["capex_per_mw"] = centers[CAPEX] / centers[POWER]
centers = centers.replace([float("inf"), float("-inf")], pd.NA)

total_power = centers[POWER].sum()
total_capex = centers[CAPEX].sum()
top10_power_share = centers.nlargest(10, POWER)[POWER].sum() / total_power
top4_owner_share = (
    centers.groupby("owner_clean")[POWER].sum().sort_values(ascending=False).head(4).sum()
    / total_power
)

owner_summary = (
    centers.groupby("owner_clean", dropna=False)
    .agg(
        power_mw=(POWER, "sum"),
        capex_b=(CAPEX, "sum"),
        h100_eq=(H100, "sum"),
        sites=("Name", "count"),
    )
    .reset_index()
    .sort_values("power_mw", ascending=False)
)
owner_summary["power_share"] = owner_summary["power_mw"] / total_power

site_rank = centers[["Name", "owner_clean", POWER, H100, CAPEX, "Country"]].dropna(subset=[POWER]).copy()
site_rank = site_rank.sort_values(POWER, ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
site_rank["rank"] = site_rank.index + 1
site_rank["cumulative_power_share"] = site_rank[POWER].cumsum() / total_power

year_rows = []
for year in range(2019, 2031):
    latest = (
        timeline[timeline["Date"] <= pd.Timestamp(f"{year}-12-31")]
        .sort_values("Date")
        .groupby("Data center")
        .tail(1)
    )
    year_rows.append(
        {
            "date": pd.Timestamp(f"{year}-12-31"),
            "year": year,
            "power_mw": latest["Power (MW)"].sum(),
            "capex_b": latest["Total capital cost (2025 USD billions)"].sum(),
            "h100_eq": latest["H100 equivalents"].sum(),
            "data_centers": latest["Data center"].nunique(),
        }
    )
yearly = pd.DataFrame(year_rows)
yearly["added_power_mw"] = yearly["power_mw"].diff().fillna(yearly["power_mw"])
yearly["record_type"] = yearly["year"].map(lambda y: "Observed / near-term" if y <= 2026 else "Planned")

events = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {
            "date": pd.Timestamp("2017-06-12"),
            "event": "Attention Is All You Need",
            "label": "Attention paper\nJun 2017",
            "label_y": yearly["power_mw"].max() * 0.70,
        },
        {
            "date": pd.Timestamp("2022-11-30"),
            "event": "ChatGPT public launch",
            "label": "ChatGPT\nNov 2022",
            "label_y": yearly["power_mw"].max() * 0.42,
        },
        {
            "date": pd.Timestamp("2023-03-14"),
            "event": "GPT-4 launch",
            "label": "GPT-4\nMar 2023",
            "label_y": yearly["power_mw"].max() * 0.58,
        },
        {
            "date": pd.Timestamp("2025-11-24"),
            "event": "OpenClaw release",
            "label": "OpenClaw\nNov 2025",
            "label_y": yearly["power_mw"].max() * 0.82,
        },
    ]
)

valid_density = centers[
    (centers[POWER] > 0)
    & centers["h100_per_mw"].notna()
    & centers[CAPEX].notna()
].copy()
median_density = valid_density["h100_per_mw"].median()
median_power = valid_density[POWER].median()
valid_density["resource_pressure"] = valid_density.apply(
    lambda row: "High power / lower density"
    if row[POWER] >= median_power and row["h100_per_mw"] < median_density
    else "Other sites",
    axis=1,
)
high_power_low_density = (
    valid_density[valid_density["resource_pressure"] == "High power / lower density"]
    .sort_values("h100_per_mw")
    .head(12)
)

continent_summary = (
    centers.groupby("continent", as_index=False)
    .agg(power_mw=(POWER, "sum"), capex_b=(CAPEX, "sum"), sites=("Name", "count"))
    .sort_values("power_mw", ascending=False)
)
continent_summary["power_share"] = continent_summary["power_mw"] / total_power

state_summary = (
    centers[centers["Country"] == "United States"]
    .groupby("state", as_index=False)
    .agg(power_mw=(POWER, "sum"), capex_b=(CAPEX, "sum"), sites=("Name", "count"))
    .sort_values("power_mw", ascending=False)
)
state_summary["power_share"] = state_summary["power_mw"] / state_summary["power_mw"].sum()
state_summary_known = state_summary[state_summary["state"] != "Unknown"]
top_state_power_share = state_summary_known.head(5)["power_mw"].sum() / state_summary_known["power_mw"].sum()
```

# Hypothesis 1

## Claim

**AI data center capacity and capital spending are concentrated among a small number of companies and projects.**

## Site Concentration

```{python}
#| echo: false
site_bars = alt.Chart(site_rank.head(20)).mark_bar(color="#3b73b9").encode(
    x=alt.X("rank:O", title="Site rank by current power"),
    y=alt.Y(f"{POWER}:Q", title="Current power (MW)"),
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("rank:O", title="Rank"),
        alt.Tooltip("Name:N", title="Data center"),
        alt.Tooltip("owner_clean:N", title="Owner"),
        alt.Tooltip(f"{POWER}:Q", title="Power (MW)", format=",.0f"),
        alt.Tooltip("Country:N", title="Country"),
    ],
)
site_line = alt.Chart(site_rank.head(20)).mark_line(
    point=True, color="#c84f2b", strokeWidth=3
).encode(
    x=alt.X("rank:O"),
    y=alt.Y("cumulative_power_share:Q", title="Cumulative share", axis=alt.Axis(format="%")),
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("Name:N", title="Data center"),
        alt.Tooltip("cumulative_power_share:Q", title="Cumulative power share", format=".1%"),
    ],
)
(site_bars + site_line).resolve_scale(y="independent").properties(
    title=alt.Title(
        "A few large sites account for much of the current footprint",
        subtitle=f"The top 10 sites represent {top10_power_share:.1%} of estimated current power.",
        anchor="start",
    ),
    height=390,
)
```

## Power vs. Capital Cost

```{python}
#| echo: false
alt.Chart(owner_summary.head(10)).mark_circle(opacity=0.78, stroke="white", strokeWidth=1).encode(
    x=alt.X("power_mw:Q", title="Estimated current power (MW)"),
    y=alt.Y("capex_b:Q", title="Estimated current capital cost (2025 USD billions)"),
    size=alt.Size("h100_eq:Q", title="H100 equivalents", scale=alt.Scale(range=[80, 1500])),
    color=alt.Color("owner_clean:N", title="Owner", scale=alt.Scale(scheme="tableau20")),
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("owner_clean:N", title="Owner"),
        alt.Tooltip("power_mw:Q", title="Power (MW)", format=",.0f"),
        alt.Tooltip("capex_b:Q", title="Capital cost ($B)", format=",.1f"),
        alt.Tooltip("h100_eq:Q", title="H100 equivalents", format=",.0f"),
    ],
).properties(
    title=alt.Title(
        "Power concentration and capital concentration move together",
        subtitle="Owner groups with the most power also carry the largest estimated capital footprint.",
        anchor="start",
    ),
    height=380,
)
```

## Result

The concentration hypothesis is supported. Owner-level and site-level views both show that aggregate infrastructure estimates are driven by a relatively small set of hyperscaler and frontier-model buildouts.

# Hypothesis 2

## Claim

**AI data center power and capital buildout accelerated after major generative AI milestones.**

## Timeline With Milestones

```{python}
#| echo: false
growth_power = alt.Chart(yearly).mark_line(point=True, strokeWidth=3).encode(
    x=alt.X("date:T", title="Year-end", axis=alt.Axis(format="%Y")),
    y=alt.Y("power_mw:Q", title="Estimated portfolio power (MW)"),
    color=alt.Color("record_type:N", title="Record type"),
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("date:T", title="Year-end", format="%Y-%m-%d"),
        alt.Tooltip("power_mw:Q", title="Power (MW)", format=",.0f"),
        alt.Tooltip("data_centers:Q", title="Data centers", format=","),
        alt.Tooltip("record_type:N", title="Record type"),
    ],
)
event_rules = alt.Chart(events).mark_rule(color="#d9822b", strokeDash=[5, 5]).encode(
    x="date:T",
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("event:N", title="Milestone"),
        alt.Tooltip("date:T", title="Date", format="%Y-%m-%d"),
    ],
)
event_labels = alt.Chart(events).mark_text(
    align="left",
    baseline="middle",
    dx=5,
    fontSize=11,
    lineBreak="\n",
    color="#8a4f13",
).encode(
    x="date:T",
    y=alt.Y("label_y:Q", title=None),
    text="label:N",
)
(growth_power + event_rules + event_labels).properties(
    title=alt.Title(
        "The buildout curve bends upward after the generative-AI inflection",
        subtitle="Milestone labels use exact event dates and align with the vertical rules.",
        anchor="start",
    ),
    height=420,
)
```


## Result

The acceleration hypothesis is supported. Estimated year-end power rises from 435 MW in 2023 to about 17,280 MW in 2026 and over 39,000 MW by 2028 in the timeline snapshot.

# Hypothesis 3

## Claim

**Data center resource intensity varies substantially by project and geography, suggesting some sites and regions may be more environmentally or operationally stressed than others.**

## Power vs. Compute Density

```{python}
#| echo: false
owner_select = alt.selection_point(fields=["owner_clean"], bind="legend")
median_rule = pd.DataFrame({"median_density": [median_density]})

scatter = alt.Chart(valid_density).mark_circle(opacity=0.76, stroke="white", strokeWidth=1).encode(
    x=alt.X(f"{POWER}:Q", title="Current power (MW)"),
    y=alt.Y("h100_per_mw:Q", title="H100 equivalents per MW"),
    size=alt.Size(f"{CAPEX}:Q", title="Capital cost ($B)", scale=alt.Scale(range=[45, 1100])),
    color=alt.Color(
        "owner_clean:N",
        title="Owner",
        scale=alt.Scale(scheme="tableau20"),
    ),
    opacity=alt.condition(owner_select, alt.value(0.82), alt.value(0.16)),
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("Name:N", title="Data center"),
        alt.Tooltip("owner_clean:N", title="Owner"),
        alt.Tooltip(f"{POWER}:Q", title="Power (MW)", format=",.0f"),
        alt.Tooltip("h100_per_mw:Q", title="H100 equivalents per MW", format=",.0f"),
        alt.Tooltip(f"{CAPEX}:Q", title="Capital cost ($B)", format=",.1f"),
    ],
).add_params(owner_select)

rule = alt.Chart(median_rule).mark_rule(color="#d9822b", strokeDash=[5, 5]).encode(
    y="median_density:Q",
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("median_density:Q", title="Median density", format=",.0f")],
)

(scatter + rule).properties(
    title=alt.Title(
        "Power does not translate into compute capacity evenly",
        subtitle=f"Dashed line marks the median: {median_density:,.0f} H100 equivalents per MW.",
        anchor="start",
    ),
    height=420,
)
```

```{python}
        anchor="start",
    ),
    height=330,
)
```

## U.S. State Concentration

```{python}
#| echo: false
alt.Chart(state_summary_known.head(15)).mark_bar().encode(
    y=alt.Y("state:N", sort="-x", title=None),
    x=alt.X("power_mw:Q", title="Estimated current power (MW)"),
    color=alt.Color("power_mw:Q", title="Power (MW)", scale=alt.Scale(scheme="viridis")),
    tooltip=[
        alt.Tooltip("state:N", title="State"),
        alt.Tooltip("sites:Q", title="Sites", format=","),
        alt.Tooltip("power_mw:Q", title="Power (MW)", format=",.0f"),
        alt.Tooltip("capex_b:Q", title="Capital cost ($B)", format=",.1f"),
        alt.Tooltip("power_share:Q", title="Share of U.S. power", format=".1%"),
    ],
).properties(
    title=alt.Title(
        "Within the U.S., power is concentrated in a handful of states",
        subtitle=f"The top five known states account for {top_state_power_share:.1%} of U.S. estimated current power with known state labels.",
        anchor="start",
    ),
    height=440,
)
```

## Result

The resource-intensity and geography hypothesis is supported. Current power is not enough to describe infrastructure impact: sites with similar power can have very different H100-equivalent density, and some high-power sites sit below the median compute-density level. The geographic views add another layer: estimated power is heavily concentrated in North America and unevenly distributed across U.S. states, which points toward regional electricity, permitting, water, and drought conditions as important follow-on context.


# OJS and Altair Together


Quarto can support python and Observable JS (OJS) cells  in the same page. Here's a little demo:

```{python}
#| height: 600

chart = (
    alt.Chart(centers).mark_bar().encode(
        y="count():Q",
        x="Current power (MW):Q",
        color = "Owner:N"
    )
)

chart

```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

ojs_define(data = centers)

```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
filtered = transpose(data).filter(function(p) {
    return p;
         
}) 
```


```{ojs}
//| title: Owner

Plot.rectY(filtered, 
  Plot.binX(
    {y: "count"}, 
    {x: "Current power (MW)", fill: "Owner", thresholds: 20}
  ))
  .plot({
    height: 600, // Set the height explicitly - otherwise quarto dashboard doesn't render right away
    marks: [
      Plot.frame(),
    ]
  }
)
```
